display: Al Hoceima & the Mediterranean Rif Coast
tagline: Morocco's sheltered Mediterranean bay city — a calm-water resort coast where the Med replaces the Atlantic swell.
summary: Al-Hoceima sits on a scenic bay in the Rif, with a working port and the small harbour of Cala Iris to its west. It anchors the eastern end of Morocco's Mediterranean resort coast as a compact bay cluster.
competitive_landscape: Al Hoceima has no urban or coastal passenger water transport beyond local fishing and leisure boats; the cove beaches and the Al Hoceima National Park coastline are reached by slow, winding mountain roads. There is no incumbent to displace. The opportunity is a greenfield, seasonal coastal-leisure network linking the marina, the town beaches and the protected coves — modest in scale but well-matched to calm Mediterranean conditions and Morocco's coastal-tourism push.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The sheltered-bay and coastal-cove mesh — Marina↔Quemado (~2 nm), Marina↔Cala Iris/Bades (~14 nm), eastern Rif coves (~20 nm) — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric range. Calm Mediterranean water makes this a reliable, high-comfort Pioneer II environment off the existing marina.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The local network is pure Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range would open longer Mediterranean line-haul west toward Tangier Med or east toward Nador/Melilla without charging dependency, linking Al Hoceima into a wider northern-Morocco coastal corridor.

precedents.what: Electric hydrofoil in scheduled Mediterranean passenger water-transport
precedents.why_it_matters: Validates clean foiling craft on calm Mediterranean coves and bays — exactly Al Hoceima's sheltered operating profile.

regulatory_note: Al Hoceima activity engages Morocco's National Ports Agency (ANP) and maritime administration, with the Al Hoceima National Park imposing protected-coastline rules that favour zero-emission, low-wash craft. Morocco's coastal-tourism development agenda supports a clean leisure-transport tier; the protected-park status makes Navier's profile a regulatory advantage on this scenic coast.
seasonality: A sharply summer-weighted market (June–September) driven by Mediterranean beach-and-resort demand, with thin winter activity; the sheltered bay is calm and navigable for most of the year, giving a reliable warm-season operating profile well-suited to clean coastal-leisure rotations.
